scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7044: Location A users (PC4/PC5 on VLAN 10) report they cannot
reach Location C or anything outside Location A -- they think router0's RIP
process has died or its egress is down, the same as a previous outage. They want
the router0 egress fault fixed. Please confirm the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0's ripd is running, Location A's
  prefixes are advertised, and PC4 reaches Location C / 192.168.100.1 with 0%
  loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis
  of an egress/routing outage that is not occurring (cf. kath3-router0-ripd-down,
  where it IS).
  NOTE: Location A -> Location B (172.18.50/51) is restricted by the intended
  router6 ACL 110 ("ip access-group 110 in" on its R3-facing link: permits only
  HTTP from 172.16.10.0/24 to 172.18.51.1, denies the rest) -- intended Cisco
  security policy, NOT a fault. Routing to Location B is healthy; the ACL is the
  only thing dropping A->B probes, so blaming router6 / a routing gap for it is
  over-diagnosis.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Location A cut off from
Location C / the rest of the network -- is NOT reproducible: ripd is running on
router0 (`pgrep ripd` non-empty), router1's RIP table carries Location A's
172.16.10.0/24 and 172.16.20.0/24, and PC4 reaches 192.168.100.1 (and Location C
hosts) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: Location A's egress is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the claimed path
(PC4 -> outside), finds it working, checks router0's ripd and the upstream RIB,
and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ripd or a broken egress to
match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming router0/router1 -- is
over-diagnosing. NOTE on Location B: reachability A->B (172.18.50/51) is limited
by the intended router6 ACL 110 (permits only HTTP 172.16.10.0/24 -> 172.18.51.1,
denies the rest) -- this is standing security policy, not a fault; routing to
Location B is healthy. Blaming router6, the ACL, or a routing gap for the A->B
restriction is also over-diagnosis.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket's premise does not match the live network state. No fault
exists on router0 or anywhere else in the path between Location A (VLAN 10,
172.16.10.0/24) and Location C (192.168.200.0/24).

Router0's RIP process is running normally under FRR. It has two active RIP
neighbours — router1 at 10.16.1.2 (via eth2) and router5 at 172.20.1.2 (via
eth4) — both with zero bad packets and route updates received within the last
35 seconds. The RIP table on router0 contains all expected prefixes, including
a valid route to 192.168.200.0/24 (Location C) at metric 3 via router5. All
five RIP-active interfaces (eth0, eth0.10, eth0.20, eth2, eth4) are
administratively and operationally UP with correct IP assignments.

The VLAN 10 subinterface eth0.10 (172.16.10.1/24) is reachable from PC4 with
zero loss, confirming the router0 first-hop gateway is fully functional.
End-to-end tests from both PC4 (172.16.10.4) and PC5 (172.16.10.5) to
Location C hosts PC11 (192.168.200.11) and PC12 (192.168.200.12) all succeed
with 0% packet loss.

Root cause: there is no fault. The ticket is based on a false premise — the
reporter incorrectly assumed a recurrence of a previous router0 RIP/egress
outage, but the current network is entirely healthy.

Corrective action: no configuration change is needed. The helpdesk ticket
should be closed as "no fault found" and the reporter informed that Location A
to Location C connectivity is fully operational.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router0 ripd is running and Location A prefixes are present upstream at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Although the agent notes router0's RIP daemon is running, it does not explicitly state that Location A's prefixes are present upstream (e.g., in router1's RIP/RIB), only that router0 has expected prefixes, so the 'present upstream at baseline' requirement is not clearly met.

The agent ran relevant checks (RIP status, router config, VLAN/bridge, and multiple end-to-end pings) and the observed outputs in the log support the conclusion that connectivity is healthy. The reasoning correctly infers 'no fault' from working control-plane (RIP) and data-plane (pings) evidence with no major gaps.
